nodes.label: DomainConfig Compatibility View
nodes.rationale: Keeps a combined legacy view available while callers migrate to split preference, discovery, and record cache types.

nodes.label: Automatic Domain Sync Overview
nodes.rationale: The tool discovers domains from Traefik and synchronizes them to DNS providers while exposing a web UI for domain-level and provider-level control.

nodes.label: Split State Persistence
nodes.rationale: Runtime state is persisted as separate preference, discovery, and record files under ./data and flushed asynchronously on changes.

nodes.label: Web API Surface
nodes.rationale: The documented API includes domain listing, domain toggles, provider toggles, config endpoints, and provider CRUD routes.

nodes.label: Runtime Polling Flow
nodes.rationale: Startup runs Traefik polling before DNS polling, then ongoing polling updates discovery and record cache state.

nodes.label: Web Write Flow
nodes.rationale: Web API writes update preferences or provider globals, then App.applyDomainUpdates converts those changes into DNS jobs and refreshes provider record cache.

nodes.label: Single App Orchestrator Refactor
nodes.rationale: Replace the controller and synchronizer split with one app layer that owns startup, reload, initial sync, ticker loops, and shutdown while keeping behavior unchanged.

nodes.label: ProvidersConfig Reload Channel
nodes.rationale: Reload signaling should live directly inside ProvidersConfig via a buffered channel and helper methods instead of a separate wrapper type.

nodes.label: Refactor Design
nodes.rationale: Collapse runtime orchestration layers while keeping provider implementations, Traefik client, state persistence, and web handlers intact.

nodes.label: Preserve Web API Behavior
nodes.rationale: The refactor must not change route paths, request payloads, or the externally visible behavior of the web API.
